A PUBLIC health expert has issued a major warning about Scotland's AI data centre boom

Now Andrew Watterson, an emeritus professor at the University of Stirling whose research has focused extensively on occupational health and safety and environmental health policies, has said Scotland is “rushing” to develop AI and that we “do not know whether we can control it or not”.

“In recent years, governments have halted energy developments because the effects on climate change had not been considered and were then found to be significant. To proceed at this stage with hyper data centres across Scotland and the rest of the UK when there may be existential threats to humanity is the height of madness.”
